title: Inverted arrows act by weak equivalences on hammock mapping spaces
statement:
Let $C$ be a small category, let $W$ be a wide subcategory, and use the reduced-hammock simplicial category $H(C,W)$ of [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation]. For any $u:x\to y$ in $W$ and $v\in C$, concatenation with the one-arrow hammock $u$ induces weak homotopy equivalences
$$H(C,W)(v,x)\longrightarrow H(C,W)(v,y),\qquad H(C,W)(y,v)\longrightarrow H(C,W)(x,v).$$
A weak homotopy equivalence means a map whose geometric realization is bijective on components and induces isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups. No freeness or calculus-of-fractions assumption is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 3.3, printed p.21. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write $R$ for reduction and write composition in functional order: $BA$ means first $A$, then $B$. Concatenating two degree-$n$ hammocks, then applying $R$, defines composition. To see explicitly that this is simplicial, a row operator $\alpha$ commutes with raw concatenation and sends each identity-column deletion or same-direction composition to the same valid reduction move. The reduction/colimit identification of [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation] therefore gives $R\alpha R(D)=R\alpha(D)$. Reducing either factor before concatenation gives the same reduced diagram as reducing the whole concatenation: the reductions of each factor are still valid moves inside it. Consequently both parenthesizations are reduction of the same three concatenated diagrams, and an empty hammock is a strict identity. For $u:x\to y$ let $a\in H(x,y)_0$ be the rightward one-arrow hammock $x\xrightarrow{u}y$, and let $b\in H(y,x)_0$ be the leftward one-arrow hammock $y\xleftarrow{u}x$, with reduction understood if $u$ is an identity. The latter is allowed because $u\in W$. A vertex used in degree $n$ means its constant $(n+1)$-row degeneracy. Composition with these constant hammocks gives simplicial maps in both variables.

source.place: Definition 2.1, printed p.19; explicit composition and row-operator verification for Proposition 3.3

proof.text: There are two cancellation edges. In $H(x,x)$ take the two-row diagram of word $+-$ whose top row is $x\xrightarrow{1_x}x\xleftarrow{1_x}x$ and whose bottom row is $x\xrightarrow{u}y\xleftarrow{u}x$. The endpoint vertical arrows are $1_x$ and the middle vertical arrow is $u:x\to y$. Both squares commute by the unit laws, all vertical arrows and both leftward arrows lie in $W$, and reduction of the top row is $1_x$. Thus this hammock gives an edge $e_x:\Delta^1\to H(x,x)$ from $1_x$ to $ba$. In $H(y,y)$ take the two-row diagram of word $-+$ whose top row is $y\xleftarrow{u}x\xrightarrow{u}y$ and bottom row is $y\xleftarrow{1_y}y\xrightarrow{1_y}y$, with endpoint vertical arrows $1_y$ and middle vertical arrow $u:x\to y$. Again both squares commute by units and all required arrows lie in $W$. It gives an edge $e_y:\Delta^1\to H(y,y)$ from $ab$ to $1_y$. These are maps from the standard simplex: at a monotone map $\theta:[n]\to[1]$ take the corresponding repeated/deleted rows of the displayed two-row hammock and reduce, as prescribed by [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation]. In particular the construction remains valid when $x=y$, when $u$ is a nonidentity endomorphism, or when $u$ is an identity.

source.place: Definition 2.1 and Proposition 3.3, printed pp.19,21; the two explicit cancellation hammocks

proof.text:
Fix $v$. Put $A=H(v,x)$ and $B=H(v,y)$, and define $P:A\to B$ by $P(D)=aD$ and $Q:B\to A$ by $Q(E)=bE$. The simplicial maps
$$A\times\Delta^1\to A,\quad(D,\theta)\longmapsto e_x(\theta)D,\qquad B\times\Delta^1\to B,\quad(E,\theta)\longmapsto e_y(\theta)E$$
are obtained by concatenating the degree-$n$ representatives and reducing. They commute with each simplicial operator by step 1; equivalently one restricts $e_x$ or $e_y$ along $\theta$, concatenates its $n+1$ rows with those of $D$ or $E$, and reduces. Their endpoint maps are respectively $1_A,QP$ and $PQ,1_B$, using associativity and the strict identity from step 1. Thus the specific target-composition map in the statement has the explicit simplicial inverse candidate $Q$ and the required endpoint homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, printed p.21, postcomposition assertion; explicit prism on arbitrary input hammocks

proof.text:
For the source-composition assertion put $A'=H(y,v)$ and $B'=H(x,v)$. Define $P':A'\to B'$ by $P'(D)=Da$ and $Q':B'\to A'$ by $Q'(E)=Eb$. The maps
$$A'\times\Delta^1\to A',\quad(D,\theta)\longmapsto D e_y(\theta),\qquad B'\times\Delta^1\to B',\quad(E,\theta)\longmapsto E e_x(\theta)$$
are simplicial by exactly the row-operator equality established in step 1. Their endpoint maps are $Q'P',1_{A'}$ and $1_{B'},P'Q'$ respectively, since $Q'P'(D)=D(ab)$ and $P'Q'(E)=E(ba)$. This writes both source-composition homotopies explicitly; no reversal of a simplicial edge is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, printed p.21, precomposition assertion; explicit prism and its two endpoint formulas

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] to each of $A,B,A',B'$. These are small simplicial sets because $C$ is small and their simplices are finite diagrams in it, modulo reduction. The natural homeomorphism $|K\times\Delta^1|\cong |K|\times[0,1]$, with its stated endpoint behavior, turns the four maps in steps 3–4 into continuous homotopies between the realizations of the indicated composites and identities. Where the identity occurs first, replace the continuous time parameter $t$ by $1-t$; this needs no simplicial reversal. Hence $|P|,|Q|$ and $|P'|,|Q'|$ are mutually inverse up to continuous homotopy. By [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak], applied separately to these two pairs, $P$ and $P'$ induce bijections on components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group. This is precisely the weak homotopy equivalence required. The cited theorem allows nonstationary basepoints and empty spaces. The only condition on $W$ used in constructing the cancellation diagrams was that it is wide and contains $u$; there was no freeness, calculus of fractions, or two-out-of-three assumption.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, printed p.21; realization and homotopy-group conclusion using the separately cited topological results

lean.statement: theorem hammock_inverted_arrow_actions {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.IsMultiplicative] {x y : C} (f : x ⟶ y) (hf : W f) (z : C) (Pzx : PresentationData W z x) (Pzy : PresentationData W z y) (Pyz : PresentationData W y z) (Pxz : PresentationData W x z) : ∃ (post : Pzx.H ⟶ Pzy.H) (pre : Pyz.H ⟶ Pxz.H), (∀ (n : ℕ) (s : Pzx.H _⦋n⦌), HammockReduces ((Pzx.simplices n s).val.comp (hammockActualPath W n f)) (Pzy.simplices n (post.app _ s)).val) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (s : Pyz.H _⦋n⦌), HammockReduces ((hammockActualPath W n f).comp (Pyz.simplices n s).val) (Pxz.simplices n (pre.app _ s)).val) ∧ Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence post ∧ Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence pre
lean.note: Uses the dependency PresentationData directly. Both induced action maps are specified in every degree by concatenating hammockActualPath and reducing; they are not arbitrary maps between the mapping simplicial sets. No freeness, fractions, saturation, nonemptiness or universe equality is assumed.
